title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on the functional equation of L-functions in the geometric case, i.e. for an l-adic sheaf E on a variety (most likely a curve) X over the finite field F_q. Grothendieck's cohomological proof, via the Lefschetz trace formula plus Poincaré duality, dates from 1964 (Bourbaki exposé 279) and SGA 5. The neighbouring 'pages' are not part of the notes: they are typed Bourbaki drafts (Algèbre commutative exercises, n° 392) whose versos he used as scrap paper, and that typing shows through on this scan.

The page records the shape of the functional equation in the following notation.

1. q = p^n (or p^ν): the cardinality of the base field.

2. ξ_E(t) is a 'completed' L-function of E. When X is not complete, it presumably includes the local factors at the missing points 'at infinity'. It also presumably carries a normalising power of t, on the order of t^{χ(E)/2}, chosen so that the equation is symmetric.

3. The boxed formula is ξ_E(1/(qt)) = A^?(t) ε'(E) ξ_E(t). The superscript on A is illegible; it may be a sign, a dual mark or an exponent. Since ξ_E appears on both sides, E is implicitly self-dual, with E^∨ ≅ E(1) up to the twist built into the variable 1/(qt). Otherwise the right side would involve the dual sheaf.

4. The correction factor is A(t) = L_E^∞(1/(qt))^{-1}: the inverse of the local L-factor at infinity, evaluated at the dual argument.

5. The constant is ε'(E) = ε(E)(-1)^{χ(E)}, where χ(E) is the Euler–Poincaré characteristic. Grothendieck first wrote ε(E) = δ(E) q^{χ(E)/2}, struck it out, and replaced it with ε(E) = δ(E) q^{-χ(E)/2}. Here δ(E) is presumably the determinant of Frobenius acting on the alternating cohomology, det(-F | H^*_c)^{±1}, so that ε(E) is the usual constant of the equation L(1/(qt)) = ε t^{χ} L(t), up to normalisation.

6. Conclusion: if X is complete, there is no correction at infinity (A(t) = 1). For self-dual E, the normalised constant is then ε'(E) = ±1: a root number of absolute value 1 that is real, hence a sign. This is the standard statement for orthogonal or symplectic self-dual sheaves on a proper curve. Duality forces δ(E)^2 = q^{χ(E)}, so δ(E) q^{-χ(E)/2} = ±1.

The page serves the bookkeeping of normalisations: the sign, the q-power and the factor at infinity.
errors: Grothendieck himself corrected a sign error in the exponent: the struck-out q^{χ(E)/2} is replaced by q^{-χ(E)/2}.
The statement ε'(E) = ±1 for complete X tacitly requires E to be self-dual (with the appropriate Tate twist) and ξ_E to be suitably normalised. These hypotheses are not written on the page.
With these notes alone, the exact definitions of ξ_E, δ(E) and the superscript on A cannot be verified, so the formula cannot be fully checked.

ideas.what: Functional equation of the L-function of an l-adic sheaf on a variety over F_q, derived from Poincaré duality and the Lefschetz trace formula
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's cohomological functional equation L(X,E,1/(qt)) = ε(E) t^{χ} L(X,E^∨,t)
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exposé 279 (Formule de Lefschetz et rationalité des fonctions L); SGA 5

ideas.what: Global epsilon constant ε(E) = δ(E) q^{-χ/2}, with δ the determinant of Frobenius on cohomology; it equals ±1 for self-dual sheaves on a proper curve
ideas.modern_name: global root number / epsilon factor; sign of the functional equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; refined into local constants by Deligne (1972-73) and Laumon (1987)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA 5 / SGA 4½ (Deligne, 'Les constantes des équations fonctionnelles des fonctions L')

ideas.what: Correction factor at infinity for non-complete X, A(t) = L_E^∞(1/(qt))^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: completed L-function including local factors at the boundary points

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine normalisation notes for the well-known cohomological functional equation and its sign. Nothing here goes beyond SGA 5 or Deligne's later work on epsilon constants.
transcription_corrections: The superscript on A in the boxed formula is unclear in the image (it looks like 'ž' or '*'). It is not clearly '?', but it remains illegible.
'q = p^n' could also be read as 'q = p^ν'.
The last line reads 'Si X complet' (the handwriting suggests 'complète'). The struck-out symbol before X is something like 'A' or 'Å'.
The struck-out first expression for ε(E) is δ(E) q^{χ(E)/2}; the corrected version is δ(E) q^{-χ(E)/2}, as transcribed.
The faint typed text visible on the scan is show-through from the Bourbaki draft on the verso; it is not part of Grothendieck's notes.
